newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Brundtland government submits resignation.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Brundtland government submits resignation.

text.p: Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland submitted her resignation as planned on Friday to pave the way for a new government to be formed under fellow-Labour Party politician Thorbjoern Jagland.
Brundtland submitted the resignation on behalf of herself and her 18-member government in a cabinet session at the Royal Palace in Oslo.

"The only thing that is sad is leaving people who have been working with you so closely," Brundtland told reporters after the session. "I think everyone who leaves a workplace they liked would say that."

Brundtland, 57, who has dominated Norwegian politics for 15 years and was premier for 10 years, said in a surprise announcement on Wednesday that she was resigning to give the party a fresh start for a general election next year.

The new prime minister, Thorbjoern Jagland, who as party leader has been groomed four years to assume the premiership, was to be sworn in with the new government in a ceremony later in the day. He has said there would be no change in Norway's policies.
